WITH bucket_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    orders.timespan,
    COUNT(*) as bucket_count
  FROM riskandmargin
  INNER JOIN orders ON riskandmargin.ordervault = orders.recordvault
  GROUP BY orders.timespan
),
bucket_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    timespan,
    bucket_count,
    SUM(bucket_count) OVER () as total_count,
    COUNT(*) OVER () as num_buckets
  FROM bucket_counts
),
bucket_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    timespan,
    bucket_count,
    total_count,
    num_buckets,
    CAST(bucket_count AS REAL) / total_count as share,
    1.0 / num_buckets as avg_share
  FROM bucket_totals
),
filtered_buckets AS (
  SELECT 
    bucket_count,
    share,
    avg_share
  FROM bucket_shares
  WHERE share > avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(bucket_count) as total_count_above_avg,
  AVG(share) as avg_share_of_above_avg,
  AVG(share - avg_share) as avg_how_far_above
FROM filtered_buckets

assumptions.assumption: Multiple risk/margin records can be associated with the same order. We count riskandmargin records by their matched order's timespan (each record contributes 1 to the count), not distinct orders.
Average share is the arithmetic mean (1 / number_of_buckets), representing what each bucket's share would be under even distribution. Buckets are above-average if their share exceeds this threshold.
